subject: POC readiness & milestone plan — network, keys, peering
messages:
From: Tracy Wong <tracy@medivex.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: NetOps <netops@medivex.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kick off: POC access & timing — Medivex evaluation

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our evaluation committee wants to get a short POC stood up so we can validate latency, cost-per-token, and private networking before the exec decision. High level asks from our side:

- Org setup + test API key for our eval account
- IP allowlist rules so our QA VMs can hit the endpoints
- VPC peering (or a secure egress path) for data flow to our internal services
- A minimal mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones & close target (we're pushing for decision by end of July)

Attached is our basic network ranges file (medivex_network_ranges.csv) and our SOC2 contact should you need it. Can you propose a concrete timeline and list of items we need to complete on our side? Also cc'ing NetOps so they can chime in with any constraints.

Thanks,
Tracy Wong
Director, Platform Engineering
Medivex Health
tracy@medivex.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Tracy Wong <tracy@medivex.com>
Cc: NetOps <netops@medivex.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kick off: POC access & timing — Medivex evaluation

Hi Tracy — great to align. I've sketched a short MAP and a recommended activation timetable and attached the draft (redwood_map_draft_v1.xlsx). High level plan below, with minimal gating items from your side: 

1) Org + API key (Day 0-1):
   - We create an evaluation org namespace and issue a scoped API key (read/write token, 72-hour TTL by default; can extend).
   - We will need the primary eval contact (name + email) and the HubSpot deal id (see related_links).

2) IP allowlist (Day 1):
   - Provide the source CIDRs your NetOps will use. We will whitelist those on our edge.
   - Typical format: 203.0.113.0/24; please confirm NAT-egress IPs for test VMs.

3) VPC peering (Day 2-4):
   - If you prefer peering, we need your AWS account ID, the VPC CIDR, and a nominated contact for route table changes.
   - Alternative: shared egress via a private load balancer with static outbound IPs — faster to stand up but not routed directly into your VPC.

4) Smoke tests & acceptance (Day 4-7):
   - We provide a short checklist (latency p95, sample token cost, request/response fidelity).

Proposed close target: July 27 (final decision). If you want an earlier SOW, we can draft a minimal DocuSign SOW and target signatures on or before July 20 to align procurement.

Next steps for you: share the CIDRs and your preferred connectivity option (peering vs. egress), and confirm the primary contact for the eval org.

I'm looping Diego (infra) for the peering details and Marcus (solutions) for the acceptance criteria.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Tracy Wong <tracy@medivex.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kick off: POC access & timing — Medivex evaluation

Hi all — a few technical notes on the peering path and what we need from Medivex NetOps. Short summary first, details below.

Summary (VPC peering preferred):
- Non-overlapping CIDRs required on both sides. Example recommended: Redwood expects to advertise 10.50.0.0/16 to the peer. Please ensure this does not conflict.
- AWS account ID + VPC ID + canonical region (us-west-2) needed.
- Route table update on your side to send traffic to the peering attachment, and a security-group rule to allow inbound from our NAT IPs (we'll provide exact IPs).
- Typical turnaround: once we receive account + VPC info + signed AUP, peering creation + acceptance + routing tends to take 24-48 hours. Plan for 72 hours for scheduling slack.

Checklist (send these items to diego@redwood.com or paste in the reply):
- AWS Account ID: xxxxxxxxxxxx
- Target VPC CIDR: e.g., 10.240.0.0/16
- Region: us-west-2
- Contact for route changes: Name, email, phone
- Any proxy/NAT in front of your VPC (Y/N)

Security note: we will not request internet-facing credentials. Peering is an infra-level change on your side to accept our peering attachment. If you prefer not to peer, we can provide a static egress IP list and TLS+mTLS endpoints as an alternate.

Also, for the test API key scope: please confirm whether you need logs exported to your Splunk/Datadog — we can wire up a temporary export to your ingest endpoint for the duration of the POC.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.com
